transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having some mornings where I wake up thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up at all. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but the thought scared me enough that I felt I should talk to someone.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
About a month now. It started after my sister died unexpectedly, and it’s been coming up since then.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do over the past month?

Not really, no. I still make myself go to things, like my book club or the dance night, but I don’t really enjoy them the way I used to. I’m there, but it feels like I’m sort of behind a pane of glass. Even things I usually love, like working in the garden or cooking something for the neighbors, just don’t give me that little lift anymore.
Have you noticed any change in your weight over the past month?
I haven’t been trying to lose weight, but food just doesn’t really appeal to me lately. I’ll make a piece of toast or some soup and then by evening realize that’s about all I’ve had.
Have you noticed any change in your energy level or how quickly you're moving compared to before your sister passed away?

Yes. I get tired much more easily now. Even simple errands, or just getting the papers together for the Cultural Center, leave me worn out. It feels like my body is moving through thick mud sometimes.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything or like you're worthless since your sister passed away?

Yes… I have. I keep going back over her last weeks and thinking I should have called more, or listened better, or done something more useful. Part of me knows I probably couldn’t have changed what happened, but I still keep blaming myself.
Have you experienced any strange sensations, heard voices, or seen things that others couldn't since your sister passed away?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that weren’t there. I’ve just been very sad and preoccupied, but nothing like that.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety, or do you feel like you're moving slower than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been especially fidgety. Maybe I’m slower with things lately, but I haven’t paid close attention to it.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower, at least not in a way I could clearly say. Maybe I take longer with things sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Do you think you've been moving slower physically since your sister passed away?
I really can’t say for sure. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower physically in any clear way. I might take longer to get going, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your friends and family since your sister passed away?

Yes, I do sometimes. I keep thinking about those last weeks with my sister, like I should have called more, or listened better, or done something more useful. Part of me knows I probably couldn’t have changed what happened, but I still feel guilty about it.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and guilt most of the day, nearly every day, since your sister passed away?

Yes… it’s been there a lot of the time. I keep going back over those last weeks with my sister and thinking I should have called more, or listened better, or done something more useful. Even when I know I probably couldn’t have changed anything, I still feel guilty about it.
How many days in the past month have you felt this way, with sadness and not enjoying things?
Almost every day, I’d say. It’s been going on for about a month now, since my sister died unexpectedly.
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt somewhat better, or has it been consistently bad every day?
It’s been pretty consistently bad, I think. Maybe there are small moments where I’m distracted, but overall this has been going on for about a month, since my sister died unexpectedly.
Have you had any significant difficulty concentrating or making decisions since your sister passed away?

Yes, I have. It’s harder to focus than usual. I’ll stare at the same budgeting spreadsheet, or reread a paragraph for a workshop three or four times, and I still don’t really take in what it says. It makes simple decisions feel slower too.
Do you feel that these feelings of sadness and guilt are interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Yes, it is. I’m not working, but with the volunteer things I do, I’ve had to ask another volunteer to cover parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop because I just can’t keep up with the preparation like I normally would. And at home, or just day to day, I’ve been turning down neighbors and friends more than usual.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I still make myself go to things, like book club or the dance night, but I don’t really enjoy them the way I used to. I’m there, but it feels like I’m sort of behind a pane of glass. Even things I normally love, like my garden or cooking for the neighbors, don’t give me that little lift anymore.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt completely unable to take care of your basic needs?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had some slow, heavy days, but I’ve still been able to get up, eat something, and take care of the basics.
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt nearly back to your normal self?
Not really. This has been going on for about a month now, since my sister died unexpectedly, and I can’t say I’ve had a day where I felt like my usual self.
Have you had any days in the past week where you felt like you couldn't get out of bed?

Not that I couldn’t get out of bed exactly. I do get up. But I feel worn out so easily—just running a simple errand or getting papers together for the Cultural Center makes me feel like I’m moving through thick mud.
